meta.title: Coach Conde — The Long Game: Athletic Edition
meta.subtitle: Speed · Power · Deceleration · Strength · Mobility · Balance
meta.tagline: Still an athlete at 33 — and still one at 63
meta.closingTagline: The goal is not to be fast at 33. It is to still be fast at 53 — and to still be here at 83.
meta.sourceDocument: Coach Conde - The Long Game Athletic Edition.pdf
meta.disclaimer: Educational training resource, not medical advice. Get medically cleared before starting, particularly before any maximal aerobic test or maximal sprint. Nutrition guidance should come from a registered dietitian. Pain that alters movement is a referral to a qualified healthcare professional, not something to train through.

clustersGlossary.description: A jump, throw or swing. Fast, light, never fatiguing. Stop the moment output drops.
The loaded movement the session is built around — hinge, squat, press.
A pull for every press, a glute movement for every hinge, an opposing pattern that lets the main work recover.
Hip, ankle or thoracic mobility, or a unilateral pattern, taken while the joint is warm.
Core as anti-movement, a balance progression, an eccentric, or a loaded carry.

executionRules: Warm-up ramp on the main lift only. Nothing else gets warm-up sets.
One set of A1. Rest the stated interval. A2. Rest. A3. Rest. A4. Rest. That is one round.
Power and speed work follow a QUALITY CAP, not a rep count. Three good jumps beat five mediocre ones, and the fifth mediocre one is where the injuries live.
If time runs short, cut a round from C. Never from A or B, and never the speed session.

loadingMethods.meaning: Percentage of your estimated max — heavy set of 5 at RIR 1, multiplied by 1.15. Round to the nearest 5 lb.
Reps In Reserve. Most sets in this program live at RIR 2-3.
Jumps, throws, sprints, plyometrics, brake work. Stop when quality drops, regardless of the prescription.

twoSafetyRules: Nothing above 80% and no true one-rep maxes.
No sprinting on cold, fatigued or under-slept legs.

blocks.name: ABSORB
blocks.strengthPowerNote: Positions, glute work, jumps kept low and landed softly
blocks.speedPlyoNote: Landing mechanics and short accelerations. Hills and sled only — no flat max-effort running.
blocks.narrative: Every session opens with a power cluster. In this block the power work is deliberately about ABSORBING force — landing well, stopping well, controlling the descent — because that is the capacity everything in Blocks 2 and 3 is built on top of.

blocks.name: BUILD
blocks.strengthPowerNote: Load added to the same patterns. Throws and bounds enter.
blocks.speedPlyoNote: Flat accelerations to 20 yards. Flying 10s. Elastic plyometrics. Reactive agility begins.
blocks.narrative: Load goes up, reps come down, and the power clusters move from absorbing force to producing it — bounds, throws, flat accelerations. Balance moves to eyes closed.

blocks.name: EXPRESS
blocks.strengthPowerNote: Contrast training — heavy set paired with a jump. Highest loads, lowest volume.
blocks.speedPlyoNote: Maximum velocity exposure. Flying 20s, 30-yard runs, full deceleration and cutting work.
blocks.narrative: The power cluster and the main lift now sit in the SAME cluster: a heavy set followed by an explosive one. That is contrast training, and it is where the strength built over eight weeks becomes speed. Bar speed governs everything — when the load stops moving fast, the cluster is finished regardless of rounds remaining.

deloadWeeksGeneric.note: Volume drops to about 60%. Written into the cards. Sprint volume halves. Landings only, no bounds.

1.warmup: RAMP: jog 3 min · leg swings · lunge walk 20 yd · A-skip 2x20 yd · build-ups 2x30 yd
1.acceleration: Hill or sled accel 4-5 x 10-15 yd

2.plyometric: Skater bound + stick 3x4 e/s · hurdle hop stick 3x4

3.plyometric: Broad jump 4x3 · single-leg bound 3x3 e/s · low depth jump 3x3 from 12"
3.acceleration: Flying 15s and 20s x4-5 · one 30 yd run in Week 11

tuesdayAmCoreBalanceBrake.title: TUESDAY AM — CORE, BALANCE & BRAKE
tuesdayAmCoreBalanceBrake.structure: Three rounds of A, two rounds of B.
tuesdayAmCoreBalanceBrake.narrative: The Brake block is the addition in this edition and it is the part that protects a thirty-three-year-old playing pickup on a Saturday.

movements.name: Dead Bug — heels to floor
movements.coachingKey: Low back pinned. If it lifts, shorten the reach.

movements.name: Single-Leg Balance
movements.coachingKey: Barefoot, hands off. The wobble is the training.

byBlock.3: 45s e/s, eyes closed on a foam pad

movements.name: Pallof Press
movements.coachingKey: Resist the rotation; the press is incidental

movements.name: BRAKE — Landing
movements.coachingKey: Three silent seconds. Knee over the foot, never inside it.

movements.name: BRAKE — Stop
movements.coachingKey: Chest over the base, hips back, short choppy final steps

movements.name: BRAKE — Redirect
movements.coachingKey: Plant wide. The cut is decided before the foot lands.

byBlock.1: Lateral shuffle to stop x4 e/w
byBlock.3: Reactive cut off a call x6

movements.name: Calf & Tibialis
movements.coachingKey: The Achilles insurance policy. Do not skip it.

byBlock.1: SL calf raise x15 e/s · tibialis x20
byBlock.2: SL calf raise x15 · pogo x15
byBlock.3: SL calf raise x20 · tibialis x25

speedRules.rule: Hills and sleds before flat ground
speedRules.detail: Resisted sprinting reduces the demand on the hamstring at the moment it is most vulnerable. Four weeks of it before flat max effort is cheap insurance at 33.
10-15 yards: 1:30 minimum. 20-30 yards: 2:30. Flying runs: 4:00. If you are breathing hard, you are conditioning, not sprinting.

speedRules.rule: Never sprint cold, tired, or under-slept
speedRules.detail: The warm-up is not optional and neither is the sleep. Sprinting is the only thing in this program with a genuinely serious downside if done badly.

speedRules.rule: Build to speed, never jump into it
speedRules.detail: Every sprint session starts with build-ups: 2x30 yards at 70%, then 2x30 at 85%, then the work.

speedRules.rule: Calves and Achilles get their own attention
speedRules.detail: Pogo hops, calf isometrics and tibialis work appear all twelve weeks. The Achilles is the tissue that ends recreational athletic careers in this age band.

speedRules.rule: If you play a sport, that counts
speedRules.detail: See the pickup-sport protocol at the back. A Saturday basketball run replaces the Thursday agility work, not adds to it.

longevityTen.name: 1.5-mile run for time
longevityTen.protocol: Flat or treadmill at 1% incline, full warm-up

longevityTen.name: Single-leg balance, eyes closed
longevityTen.protocol: Barefoot, hands on hips, best of 2

longevityTen.name: Sit-to-rise
longevityTen.protocol: Start at 10, subtract 1 point per support hand/limb used getting up and down from the floor

longevityTen.name: Trap-bar deadlift E1RM
longevityTen.protocol: Heavy set of 5 at RIR 1, estimated 1RM = weight x 1.15 (round to nearest 5 lb)

longevityTen.name: Side plank
longevityTen.protocol: Each side; record the difference between sides

longevityTen.name: Shoulder flexion at the wall
longevityTen.protocol: Low back flat against wall, arms overhead

athleticFive.name: 10-yard sprint
athleticFive.protocol: Two-point start, phone timing app or timing gates. 3 attempts, full recovery between.
athleticFive.caution: If you have not run fast since your twenties, DO NOT test this at Week 0. Run Block 1 first and test at Week 6.

athleticFive.name: Standing broad jump
athleticFive.protocol: Two feet, arm swing allowed, measured to the nearest heel. 3 attempts.

athleticFive.name: Countermovement jump
athleticFive.protocol: Hands on hips or arm swing — pick one and never change it. 3 attempts.
athleticFive.note: Arm-swing method choice must be locked at Week 0 and reused every retest.

athleticFive.name: 10-to-5 Deceleration Deficit
athleticFive.protocol: Sprint-and-stop time minus sprint-through time, both measured over 10 yards

week0.label: Week 0 Baseline
week0.note: Complete baseline test for all 15 markers, finished before Week 1 begins. Get medically cleared first, particularly before the 1.5-mile test and before any maximal sprint, if largely inactive, carrying cardiovascular risk factors, or not having sprinted in years.

schedulingRules.restingHeartRate: Marker #1 protocol requires morning-before-rising readings averaged over 3 days (per the Longevity Ten protocol) — Week 0 testing necessarily spans at least 3 calendar days for this marker alone.
schedulingRules.athleticFive: Markers #11-15 must be tested together on a separate, fresh day, after a full warm-up and build-ups. Never at the end of another session and never on tired legs (per the Athletic Five protocol).
schedulingRules.sprintDeferral: If the athlete has not run fast since their twenties, DO NOT test marker #11 (10-yard sprint) at Week 0 — defer it to Week 6, once four weeks of hills/sled work (Block 1) have prepared the tissue. Markers #12-15 are still tested at Week 0 as normal; only #11 is deferred.

suggestedSchedule.note: The source PDF does not prescribe exact Week 0 weekdays (unlike Week 6 and Week 12, which do). This is an app-suggested default only, modeled on the Week 12 3-day test-week format — athletes/coaches may reorder or spread it across more days, as long as the resting-heart-rate 3-morning window and the Athletic-Five fresh-day rule above are respected.

days.what: Begin resting heart rate collection (#1). Optionally pair with the other quick Longevity Ten markers: grip strength (#3), single-leg balance eyes closed (#4), sit-to-rise (#5), deep squat hold (#6), shoulder flexion at the wall (#10).
Resting heart rate, reading 3 of 3 — baseline RHR is now the 3-morning average.

days.suggestedDay: Athletic Five day (separate, fresh, full warm-up)
days.what: 10-yard sprint (#11, unless deferred — see sprintDeferral above), standing broad jump (#12), countermovement jump (#13), 5-10-5 (#14), 10-to-5 deceleration deficit (#15). Full recovery between everything. Nothing else that day.
Trap-bar deadlift E1RM (#7, heavy set of 5 at RIR1 x1.15), push-ups to technical failure (#8), side plank (#9). The 1.5-mile run (#2) can be placed here or on its own day.

week6.label: Week 6 Mid-Program Retest

conditionalMarkers.condition: Add the 10-yard sprint ONLY when it was deferred at Week 0 (see week0.schedulingRules.sprintDeferral). Four weeks of hills/sled work have by now prepared the tissue for it.

week6.note: PARTIAL retest — exactly the six markers specified in the PDF: resting heart rate (#1), single-leg balance eyes closed (#4), sit-to-rise (#5), side plank (#9), standing broad jump (#12), and the 10-to-5 deceleration deficit (#15), plus the conditional 10-yard sprint (#11) above. This is intentional per the PDF. Do NOT treat Week 6 as a complete 15-marker retest, and do not present it to the user as one.

week12.label: Week 12 Final Test — full taper and test week

schedule.what: AM: landings 2x5, 2x10 yd at 90%, 15 min easy. PM: Strength A at the deload (Wk12) column.
AM: core, balance and brake at Block 1 volume (NOT Block 3 — an explicit taper override). PM: Strength B at the deload (Wk12) column.
TEST DAY 1 — health markers: resting HR (#1), grip (#3), balance eyes closed (#4), sit-to-rise (#5), deep squat hold (#6), shoulder flexion (#10).

TEST DAY 2 — THE ATHLETIC FIVE (#11-15). Full warm-up and build-ups first. 10-yard sprint, broad jump, CMJ, 5-10-5, 10-to-5 deceleration deficit. Full recovery between everything. Nothing else that day.
TEST DAY 3 — trap-bar 5RM estimate (#7), push-ups (#8), side plank (#9). Then 30 minutes easy. The 1.5-mile run (#2) goes here if you want it separated from the sprint day.
Off. Put the numbers next to Week 0 and decide what the next twelve weeks emphasize.

week12.note: Thursday and Saturday PM strength (Strength C, Strength D) are not prescribed this week — replaced by testing.

maxRecalculation.rule: Re-estimate maxes at Week 8, not before.
maxRecalculation.howSpecifiedInPdf: Not explicitly detailed as a formal protocol — flagged in EXTRACTION_AUDIT.md.
maxRecalculation.appDefault: Offer an 'Update Estimated Max' action on trap-bar deadlift, back squat, and bench press starting Week 8, using the same E1RM formula (heavy set of 5 at RIR1 x1.15, rounded to nearest 5 lb) applied to that week's B1 working set.

pickupSportRules.action: That game replaces the Thursday AM agility work. Everything else stays. Lift the day AFTER the game, not the day before.
Drop the Monday AM speed session to landings and build-ups only. The games supply your sprint exposure. Keep all four lifts.
Move Strength D to Sunday or drop its C cluster. Saturday AM becomes a warm-up, not a long run.

pickupSportRules.situation: You have not played in months
pickupSportRules.action: Do not go back to a competitive game until you have finished Block 1. Four weeks of landings, hills and sled work first.
Full RAMP warm-up plus build-ups: 2x30 yd at 70%, 2x30 at 85%, 2x20 yd at 90%, and five drop-and-sticks. Ten minutes.
Walk it out, hydrate, sleep. The next session drops one RIR column.

progressionRules.rule: Percentage lifts: the card tells you. Re-estimate maxes at Week 8, not before.
RIR lifts: add the smallest available increment when you hit the top of the rep range at the stated RIR for all sets, two sessions running.
Jumps and throws: progress by intent and quality, never by adding reps. A higher jump at three reps beats the same jump at six.
Sprints: progress distance before intensity, and resisted before flat. Never add both in the same week.
Plyometrics: progress absorb → elastic → express, in that order, and only when the landing is silent and the knee tracks over the foot.
Balance: progress by removing information — eyes, then the stable surface — not by adding time.

substitutions.useInstead: Stadium steps, a treadmill at 8-10% incline, or a resistance band held by a partner
A bike or rower for the aerobic work, plus hill walking. But find somewhere to sprint — it is the least substitutable thing here.
Barbell RDL or double-DB deadlift from blocks
DB hip thrust, single-leg hip thrust, or heavy banded glute bridge
Goblet squat, safety-bar squat, heel-elevated front squat
A light dumbbell for the rotational pattern, or a heavy band for the throw pattern
A cone, a rolled towel, a line on the floor. The height is not the point — the landing is.

substitutions.missing: A joint that hurts in a movement
substitutions.useInstead: Do not work around pain that changes how you move. Physio referral, not substitution.

backOffSignals.signal: Resting heart rate up more than about 7 bpm for three straight mornings
backOffSignals.response: Take the deload column this week. Keep the AM sessions, cut the C clusters, no sprinting.

backOffSignals.signal: Calf or Achilles tightness, soreness or a "twinge"
backOffSignals.response: No sprinting and no plyometrics until it is fully clear for 72 hours. This is the warning shot; the rupture is what comes next if it is ignored.
No speed session that day. Lift at RIR 4, skip the C cluster.

backOffSignals.signal: A hamstring that feels "grabby" during build-ups
backOffSignals.response: End the sprint session there. Do the easy run instead. Return to hills for a week before flat sprinting again.

backOffSignals.signal: Joint pain that changes how you move
backOffSignals.response: Stop and get it looked at. At 33 the small things fixed early are the ones that never become chronic.
Restart at the beginning of the block you were in. Do not resume sprinting where you left off.

recoveryPrinciples: Sleep is the intervention. Seven to nine hours, consistent times. It outperforms every supplement and most training decisions, and it matters more in this edition because sprinting is a nervous-system cost as much as a muscular one.

Protein spread across the day. For an adult doing resistance training, commonly cited intakes sit around 1.6-2.2 g per kg of bodyweight daily; a registered dietitian can tell you what fits you specifically.
Carbohydrate around sessions. Two-a-days on low fuel is how the PM session quietly becomes worthless.
Walk on off days. Twenty to thirty minutes.
Cold plunges after strength work may blunt the adaptation you just trained for. Use them for acute recovery, not habitually.
